transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-02
Time: 15:00 PT (scheduled 45m, ran 49m)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM) -- Marcus Lee (Peregrine Head of Platform), Nina Patel (Peregrine SRE), Jonah Rivera (CTO), Laila Osman (Procurement), Samir Kaur (Security)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in. Customer evaluating capacity uplift (more GPUs/dedicated pool), adding APAC region (Singapore) and looking at contract term (12 vs 24 mo). Security and procurement questions surfaced (SOC2/P2P, SSO, KMS). Action items and a benchmark request agreed.

Topics:
- Current usage and headroom
- Dedicated capacity pricing and burst options
- APAC region onboarding timeline and data residency
- Security artifacts (SOC2, ISO, KMS integration)
- Next steps: quote, benchmark, network diagrams, procurement PO timeline

Transcript (timestamps approximate, auto-transcribed, occasional errors):
[00:00] Alyssa: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, this is Alyssa from Redwood. quick agenda — renewal cadence, proposed uplift, apac region timeline, and any security/procurement blockers. Diego's here for the technical bits.
[00:12] Marcus: thanks, Alyssa. we are on a tight calendar — finance wants to lock a vendor by mid april if possible. we' re at about 75% of our current reserved pool right now but we see spikes on euro and apac hours.
[00:22] Nina: yeah the midnight run for reconciliations kicks up qps. most requests are short, but tail latency matters for a couple of endpoints.
[00:31] Diego: got it. do you have percentile target? p95, p99?
[00:35] Nina: p95 <= 180 ms ideally, p99 < 400 ms for our critical flows.
[00:40] Diego: ok that's doable with a dedicated pool plus a small hot standby burst. the trade is cost. we can tune batching and kv cache to keep tokens down.
[00:49] Marcus: and that's where we are debating hosted vs dedicated — we like predictable perf for reconciliation and fraud checks. procurement leaned dedicated for SLAs.
[00:58] Alyssa: perfect, so main asks — uplift capacity (reserve more GPUs), add APAC region (singapore) for lower latency, extend to a 12- or 24-month contract for better unit pricing.
[01:09] Laila: from procurement side we need an enterprise addendum and clarity on termination, data retention, and any pass-through costs.
[01:16] Samir: security wants SOC2 type 2 and details on KMS/HSM integration, we use AWS KMS in our account and need to know key policies.
[01:25] Alyssa: we can send SOC2 attestation, and we do support customer-managed KMS in private deployments; for Dedicated it's an option depending on the plan. we'll include the exact HSM/KMS notes in the security pack.
[01:35] Jonah: about APAC, how long to provision and what's required from us?
[01:39] Diego: provisioning a new region for Dedicated typically takes 3-6 weeks; shorter if there's pre-provisioned capacity. we need a small network change — a peering/VPC setup and sample traffic to validate egress. also we recommend a canary period.
[01:52] Nina: can you run a benchmark with our test corpus? we want to see both latency and cost per 1k tokens numbers.
[01:58] Diego: yes, we can run a throughput + latency run with your anonymized set on a mirrored dedicated pool. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost given quantization profiles.
[02:08] Marcus: also want to understand fallback behavior — if apac pool is saturated, will traffic route to eu or na? what's the failover impact on latency and cost?
[02:18] Diego: smart routing will fallback to nearest compatible model/region and we can policy it by latency or cost. you can set hard SLOs to prefer latency. fallback may increase token egress and cost but keeps the app online.
[02:32] Alyssa: quick note on pricing — we can propose a tiered commitment: small uplift + burst credits for immediate spikes, or larger reserved commitment for lower per-token. we also have a short-term pilot for private on-prem if you need air-gapped.
[02:46] Laila: procurement will push back on multi-year unless there are price protections and clear ROI.
[02:50] Alyssa: understood. typically we model savings on per-token and e2e latency improvements; we'll include examples in the quote.
[02:57] Samir: about logs and audit — do you provide per-request audit logs and how long are they retained by default?
[03:03] Priya: yes audit logs available; default retention is 90 days on hosted, longer on enterprise add-on. we can include retention SLAs in dedicated/private deals.
[03:12] Marcus: any known competitors that do this cheaper? we've had internal folks look at CloudAI and FastServe.
[03:17] Alyssa: yes, we've seen those — CloudAI has lower headline per-token in some cases but lacks the unified private/dedicated interface and more advanced batching/caching optimizations. we'll call out direct differences in the one-pager.
[03:28] Nina: ok, for the benchmark, what access do you need from us?
[03:31] Diego: a redacted corpus (we can accept anonymized synthetic), a sample of typical request size distribution, and expected peak qps by hour. also network egress details so we can simulate realistic latency.
[03:43] Marcus: we can get that to you. timeline-wise, if you run the benchmark early next week that helps procurement and infra decisions.
[03:50] Alyssa: will do. Diego, can you also include result columns for p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens across quant profiles?
[03:56] Diego: yep, and I'll include throughput numbers and sample config used (batch size, kv cache settings).
[04:03] Laila: procurement needs a sample contract language for indemnity and data residency.
[04:08] Alyssa: we'll attach a redlined sample and the enterprise addendum.
[04:12] Samir: one more on keys — if we move to VPC/private, can we keep our KMS keys?
[04:17] Diego: in private and many Dedicated setups, yes, you can manage keys. we'll walk through key policies; for hosted API we do encryption at rest but not customer-managed KMS.
[04:26] Jonah: what about rollout strategy? we want to start with fraud endpoints, then expand.
[04:30] Priya: recommended canary: 10% traffic to start for 1 week, monitor latency and error rates, then 50% for a week, etc. we'll provide a rollout checklist in the follow-up.
[04:41] Marcus: timeline: if we sign by 15th, can we get APAC by end of May?
[04:45] Diego: tight but feasible; depends on whether you pick reserved capacity vs burst. reserved pool with pre-warm can be online in ~3 weeks, otherwise 5-6.
[04:55] Alyssa: recap of action items and next steps: we'll send a 12-month and 24-month quote with scenarios, Diego will run benchmark, Peregrine will send network diagrams and sample corpus, schedule VPC/security review for week of 4/11.
[05:07] Marcus: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:10] Alyssa: thanks, we'll follow up with docs and next steps.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearing on acronyms (K-V written as kay vee) and punctuation.

Referenced artifacts / links (to be attached in follow-up):
- Renewal quote template (link to Redwood pricing sheet)
- Dedicated pool config checklist (doc)
- SOC2 attestation PDF and security one-pager
- Benchmark results template (sheet)

End of meeting.
